\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{একেবারে} (ekebāre)}{একেবারে (ekebāre)}]{\bn{একেবারে} (ekebāre) — completely; absolutely}

\label{lesson:BN-C373-ekebare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a level, then the Bengali for an amount.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{একেবারে}}
\textbf{\bn{একেবারে}} — \emph{ekebāre} — \textquotedblleft{}completely; absolutely\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{এই} \bn{রাস্তায়} \bn{গেলে} \bn{আমরা} \bn{একেবারে} \bn{ঠিক} \bn{সময়ে} \bn{পৌঁছাব।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ei rāstāy gele āmrā ekebāre ṭhik sômôye poũchhābô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If we take this road, we'll arrive exactly on time.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{একেবারে}} (\emph{ekebāre}) is \bn{এক}, one (CDIAL 2462), with \bn{বার}, a time or turn, and the Bengali -\bn{এ}: 'all at one go', so completely. With \bn{না} it means 'not at all'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ekebāre}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ekebāre}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ei rāstāy gele āmrā ekebāre ṭhik sômôye poũchhābô.} — If we take this road, we'll arrive exactly on time.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a level, then the Bengali for an amount, then say \emph{ekebāre} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{একেবারে} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Completely; absolutely\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সম্পূর্ণ} (sômpūrnô)}{সম্পূর্ণ (sômpūrnô)}]{\bn{সম্পূর্ণ} (sômpūrnô) — complete; entire}

\label{lesson:BN-C373-sompurno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for an amount, then the Bengali for absolutely.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সম্পূর্ণ}}
\textbf{\bn{সম্পূর্ণ}} — \emph{sômpūrnô} — \textquotedblleft{}complete; entire\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{কাজটা} \bn{সম্পূর্ণ} \bn{হলে} \bn{আমি} \bn{টাকা} \bn{দেব।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kājṭā sômpūrnô hôle āmi ṭākā debô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I'll pay when the work is complete.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সম্পূর্ণ}} (\emph{sômpūrnô}) is Sanskrit \emph{sampūrṇa}, filled right up (Monier-Williams): complete, with nothing missing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sômpūrnô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sômpūrnô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kājṭā sômpūrnô hôle āmi ṭākā debô.} — I'll pay when the work is complete.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for an amount, then the Bengali for absolutely, then say \emph{sômpūrnô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{অন্তত} (ôntôtô)}{অন্তত (ôntôtô)}]{\bn{অন্তত} (ôntôtô) — at least}

\label{lesson:BN-C373-ontoto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for absolutely, then the Bengali for complete.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{অন্তত}}
\textbf{\bn{অন্তত}} — \emph{ôntôtô} — \textquotedblleft{}at least\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{অন্তত} \bn{দশজন} \bn{এলে} \bn{সভা} \bn{হবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ôntôtô dôshjôn ele sôbhā hôbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The meeting will go ahead if at least ten people come.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{অন্তত}} (\emph{ôntôtô}) is Sanskrit \emph{antatas}, 'from the end', which Monier-Williams also gives as 'in the lowest way': counting from the bottom, at the very least.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôntôtô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôntôtô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôntôtô dôshjôn ele sôbhā hôbe.} — The meeting will go ahead if at least ten people come.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for absolutely, then the Bengali for complete, then say \emph{ôntôtô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{অন্তত} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}At least\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{প্রায়} (prāy)}{প্রায় (prāy)}]{\bn{প্রায়} (prāy) — almost; nearly}

\label{lesson:BN-C373-pray}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for complete, then the Bengali for at least.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{প্রায়}}
\textbf{\bn{প্রায়}} — \emph{prāy} — \textquotedblleft{}almost; nearly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{কাজ} \bn{প্রায়} \bn{শেষ}; \bn{কাল} \bn{এলে} \bn{দেখবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāj prāy shesh; kāl ele dekhbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The work is almost finished; if you come tomorrow, you'll see.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{প্রায়}} (\emph{prāy}) is Sanskrit \emph{prāya}, 'for the most part, almost' (Monier-Williams). With the ending -\bn{ই} it gives the taught \bn{প্রায়ই}, often.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prāy}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prāy}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāj prāy shesh; kāl ele dekhbe.} — The work is almost finished; if you come tomorrow, you'll see.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for complete, then the Bengali for at least, then say \emph{prāy} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{প্রায়} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Almost; nearly\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{আংশিক} (āngshik)}{আংশিক (āngshik)}]{\bn{আংশিক} (āngshik) — partial; in part}

\label{lesson:BN-C373-angshik}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for at least, then the Bengali for nearly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{আংশিক}}
\textbf{\bn{আংশিক}} — \emph{āngshik} — \textquotedblleft{}partial; in part\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{জল} \bn{কম} \bn{থাকলে} \bn{কারখানা} \bn{আংশিক} \bn{বন্ধ} \bn{থাকবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jôl kôm thākle kārkhānā āngshik bôndhô thākbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If water is short, the factory will be partly shut.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{আংশিক}} (\emph{āngshik}) is built on Sanskrit \emph{aṃśa}, a share or part (Monier-Williams), with the adjective ending \emph{-ika}: 'in part'. The adjective itself is a later formation.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āngshik}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āngshik}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jôl kôm thākle kārkhānā āngshik bôndhô thākbe.} — If water is short, the factory will be partly shut.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for at least, then the Bengali for nearly, then say \emph{āngshik} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{আংশিক} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Partial; in part\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
